title: No Nails Hold Up This Roof — China's 2,500-Year Secret | China Travel Expert
description:
Walk into an old Chinese hall, look up under the wide eaves, and you'll see the trick: the huge roof is carried without a single nail.

The secret is 斗拱 (dougong) — sets of interlocking wooden brackets. A block (dou) sits on each column, a bracket arm (gong) slots into it, and layer by layer they carry the roof out over the walls — no nails, no glue, just precisely cut mortise-and-tenon joints. The system is roughly 2,500 years old, and because the joints can flex instead of snapping, it lets timber buildings sway through an earthquake. It's the same principle that has helped Beijing's Forbidden City ride out around 200 earthquakes in 600 years.

🧭 Expert Tip: At any palace or temple, stand under the eaves and look straight up — the stacked, painted brackets fanning out from each column are the dougong doing all the work.

一根钉子都不用,一朵朵斗拱把大屋顶稳稳托起来。
